history.body: Hi, we have a young child and our rental is getting a bit tight. Is the 3-bedroom layout practical for a small family?

It could be practical for a small family. The Type A is 900 sq ft with 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, so you could have a separate room for your child while still having space to spend time together in the open-plan living and dining area. The layout also avoids a long corridor and includes a small storage area. I’d recommend viewing it to judge the room sizes and layout for yourselves; exact furniture fit should be checked against the approved plan.
That sounds more workable than what we have now. Is there a place for kids to play in the development?

There’s an approximately 10-acre landscaped facilities deck on Level 9, giving residents a substantial shared outdoor green space. I don’t have verified details on whether there’s a dedicated children’s playground or play equipment, so I’ll check that specifically for you.
A green space could still be useful. Do you know if kids can use it to play, or would that depend on the facilities rules?

The development’s facilities list does include a playground, alongside the roughly 10-acre landscaped Level 9 facilities deck. I can’t confirm whether the playground is on that deck or the specific access and supervision rules; use of the facilities would be subject to the management rules. The green space could still give your family an outdoor area to enjoy together.
That sounds worth seeing for ourselves. Could we visit this weekend?

Yes, I’ll pass your request to our salesperson to coordinate a visit this weekend and confirm an available time with you. It isn’t booked until they confirm. You’ll be able to assess the three-bedroom layout and room sizes in person.
